resources.string: Set up the access needed so monitoring, performance controls, and floating features work as intended.
Complete Root access and the required permissions to continue.
AetherX needs superuser approval to run the supported system controls. The request will appear from a root manager such as Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch. Review the request before approving it.
Complete the access on this step first to continue.
Review the previous steps, complete all permissions, then confirm you understand the kernel risks.
Access is ready. You can move on to the next step.

On some devices, battery saver can stop AetherX processes while the app isn\'t visible. This exception is optional, but it can help root services and monitoring keep running more consistently. You can change it back anytime in system settings.

This is AetherX\'s main access. Root is required to apply system tweaks and performance controls that run at the device level. Make sure Magisk, KernelSU, or APatch is installed and root works before approving the request.

Android asks for this special permission so AetherX can change certain system settings the app supports. This permission is separate from Root and doesn\'t change any settings by itself; only the related features use it when you run them.
Open AetherX\'s system permission page and enable “Allow modifying system settings”.

This permission lets floating elements, such as the crosshair or in-game monitor, appear on top of games. Enable it only if you want to use overlay features; you can still manage this permission later in Android Settings.
Enable the display-over-other-apps permission so overlay features can be used.

Notifications help Android show the status of running services and important messages from AetherX. On Android versions that ask for this permission, you can enable it here; the notification permission doesn\'t give access to change the system.
Allow notifications so service status can be shown clearly.
Understand the risks of kernel settings
Kernel Manager can change CPU and GPU behavior. Wrong settings can make the device unstable, overheat, or restart. Read the points below before continuing.
Governors and frequencies determine how the CPU/GPU behave. Values that don\'t suit your device can cause lag, freezes, crashes, or reboots. Change one setting at a time and note the original value.
Don\'t disable thermal protection. Letting components overheat can reduce performance, damage the device, or shorten the life of the battery and components.
Support and effects of each option differ per device, kernel, and ROM. Make sure you understand the changes you make, have a way to restore the original values, and proceed at your own risk.
I understand the risks and will change kernel settings carefully.
